metadata.title: Claude, Creating Financial Models.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude building a DCF or running a sensitivity table is general financial judgment or something more specific, using the creating-financial-models skill's own description as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a financial-modeling skill is SKILL.md, a spec Claude reads and runs the same way against whatever numbers you hand it.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (hand the skill a five-year revenue projection: same three steps run every time; then the same pipeline runs identically twice, and just as readily against a projection outside the spec)

beats.narration_text: Someone wonders how you'd teach Claude to build financial models. But Claude isn't trained for this — it's pointed at a skill it reads before acting. So: how do you point it at one?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works — not something it's trained on. This one is creating-financial-models: dcf_model.py, sensitivity_analysis.py, and a four-kilobyte SKILL.md holding the full instruction set, plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads the file, then acts. The file is the program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder opening to three files, SKILL.md highlighted; 'not trained on it' callout; 'the file is the program' closer

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens into three file rows: dcf_model.py (16k), sensitivity_analysis.py (11k), and SKILL.md (4k) — SKILL.md recolors teal and grows slightly. A 'not trained on it' tag crosses out a brain glyph. Closing line: 'the file is the program'.

beats.narration_text: The instructions sit in a Steps section: read each step in order, execute it, return the result — linear, no branching unless a step says so. Watch the anchor. Hand the skill a five-year revenue projection: it reads the assumptions, runs dcf_model.py, and hands back a valuation. Same three steps, every time.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — three linear pipeline phases, then a revenue projection arrowing through dcf_model.py to a valuation output

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — a revenue projection, three steps
production_viz.mechanic: Three phase cards appear left to right and connect with arrows: 'read SKILL.md' / 'execute' / 'return result'. They fade back. THE ANCHOR. A card labelled 'revenue projection' arrows into a card labelled 'dcf_model.py', which arrows into a card labelled 'valuation out'. Closing line beneath: 'same three steps, every time'. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Same input, same output, every run — hand it the identical revenue projection twice and dcf_model.py returns the identical valuation both times. That's the payoff of a file being the program. But the reverse holds too: hand it a projection the steps weren't written for, and it still runs those same steps — against numbers the SKILL.md never specified. The limit is the spec: DCF analysis, sensitivity testing, Monte Carlo simulations, scenario planning — and nothing outside it.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same pipeline firing identically twice, then split: identical projection twice = identical valuation; projection outside the spec = same steps still run; closing spec list

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same input, same output; then the limit
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 PIPELINE RETURNS, identical, running twice in a row — two matching 'valuation out' cards appear side by side, labelled 'same input, same output'. Then it splits: left card 'in-spec projection' → pipeline → clean valuation, labelled 'the payoff'; right card 'projection outside the spec' → the same pipeline → valuation computed anyway, labelled 'the limit'. Closing line: 'DCF · sensitivity · Monte Carlo · scenario planning — nothing outside it'.

beats.narration_text: A financial-modeling skill isn't Claude inventing a model from judgment — it's SKILL.md, a spec Claude reads and runs the same way against whatever numbers you hand it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want to stress-test a five-year revenue projection. Read the creating-financial-models skill and walk me through what you will build before you touch a number. Watch for that clause — before you touch a number — that's the discipline the spec enforces: the plan is visible before the model runs. Liam, in for Bear.
